summary: A 1922-23 D-1 log cupola cabin on Hornet Mountain in Flathead National Forest, staffed 1923-1946, later abandoned and then restored as a rental cabin.

facts.design: D-1 style log cupola cabin, 14x14 ft single-room log cabin, saddle-notched logs
facts.status_note: Restored after years of abandonment; now a Forest Service rental cabin

access.note: Open as a paid Recreation.gov rental; narrow access road (FS Road 9805)

visit.trail_note: Reached by road (Hornet Road 9805), described as narrow with few pullouts

events.note: Construction began 1922, completed 1923, in response to the 1910 fires
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, August 19, 1983
A wildfire burned the surrounding area in 2003; the lookout itself survived
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, November 27, 2016

evidence.supports: location on Hornet Mountain in Flathead National Forest, ~45 miles north of Columbia Falls
evidence.quote: Hornet Lookout is a former fire lookout tower located in the Flathead National Forest and is located approximately 45 miles (72 km) north of Columbia Falls, Montana.
Hornet Lookout was constructed between 1922 and 1923 as a response to the great fire of 1910.
Hornet Lookout was constructed by US Forest Service seasonal employees at a cost of $719.38. All materials were either available on the site or were packed in by trail.

evidence.supports: design details: D-1 style, 14x14 log cabin, saddle-notched logs, interior furnishings
evidence.quote: Hornet Lookout is a D-l style US Forest Service fire lookout tower situated on the summit of Hornet Mountain. The building is a 14' by 14' single room log cabin. The cabin is made of 8-10 inch logs which are saddlenotched at the corners. The interior of the structure contains built-in storage containers, a wood burning stove, two bed frames and a hand crafted chair.
The words "Hornet L.O." are spelled out in white painted rocks. The letters are approximately 4 ft. high and are located approximately 75 ft. to the east of Hornet Lookout.
The lookout was staffed each summer from 1923 until approximately 1946.

evidence.supports: abandoned for years, then restored, now available for rental
evidence.quote: Hornet Peak Lookout was built in 1922. It has a D-1 log cupola cabin. While it was abandoned for a number of years, it has now been restored and available for rental.

evidence.supports: 2003 wildfire burned surrounding area, vegetation regrowing
evidence.quote: The rustic lookout was built in 1922 and, in its prime, played an integral role for detecting forest fires in the North Fork area. A 2003 wildfire charred the surrounding area, but wildflowers and bear grass are making a comeback.

evidence.supports: available to rent mid-June to October
evidence.quote: Hornet Lookout is available to rent from mid-June to October annually.
The cost to rent the lookout is $40 per night.

evidence.supports: two-story structure, cabin amenities, no running water
evidence.quote: The two-story lookout sits at ground level. The ground level provides a living space for two guests and the second story is a small loft used solely for full views of the region. The lookout's rustic accommodations include a propane cook stove, propane lantern, two cots, a small wood stove for heat.

evidence.supports: no water available, pack in own supplies
evidence.quote: No water is available. Guests should pack their own bedding, water, first aid kit and food, among other necessities.

evidence.supports: narrow access road with few pullouts
evidence.quote: Use caution; Hornet Road 9805 is narrow, with few pullouts.

notes_for_editor: Good agreement across NHLR, Wikipedia (citing the NRHP nomination), and Recreation.gov. No source gives an exact date for when staffing ended besides 'approximately 1946' or exactly when restoration occurred, only that it was 'abandoned for a number of years' before restoration.
